name: Stop Edge feature tips and suggestions
summary: No pop-ups that suggest Edge features.
what: Applies the Edge policy that turns off feature recommendations and browser assistance notifications.
benefit: No dialogs, flyouts or banners nudging you to try Edge features, such as vertical tabs when many tabs are open.
risk: None. Every feature is still in Edge settings. Edge may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested for everyone who finds the prompts distracting.
facts: Covers dialogs, flyouts, coach marks and banners inside Edge
Applies to every account
Revert removes the policy value

name: Hide Microsoft Rewards in Edge
summary: No Rewards points, icon or notifications in Edge.
what: Applies the Edge policy that hides the Microsoft Rewards experience and switches its setting off.
benefit: No Rewards prompts or notifications on the new tab page and in search while you use Edge.
risk: Low. You stop collecting Rewards points through Edge. Edge may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested if you do not collect Microsoft Rewards points. Skip it if you do.
facts: Affects Microsoft account users in markets where Rewards is offered
Takes effect after Edge restarts
Applies to every account
Revert removes the policy value

name: Skip Edge's welcome screens
summary: No first-run tour or splash screen for a new Edge profile.
what: Applies the Edge policy that hides the first-run experience and the splash screen.
benefit: A new Edge profile opens straight to the browser, with no tour or sign-in and sync pitch.
risk: Low. Sync stays off until you turn it on, and Edge asks about it when it starts.
advice: Handy if you set up Edge on several accounts or PCs. Skip it if you want the guided setup.
facts: The new tab page uses the MSN News feed and the Inspirational layout
A Windows account that is a work, school or Microsoft account still signs in to Edge
Takes effect after Edge restarts
Revert removes the policy value

name: Turn off Edge feedback and surveys
summary: Edge can no longer open its feedback tool.
what: Applies the Edge policy that disables Edge Feedback, which Edge uses for suggestions, issue reports and customer surveys.
benefit: No feedback or survey requests from inside Edge.
risk: None. You can still report an Edge problem through Windows Feedback Hub. Edge may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested if you never send feedback to Microsoft from Edge.
facts: Without the policy, Edge Feedback is on and cannot be turned off in Edge
Takes effect after Edge restarts
Applies to every account
Revert removes the policy value

name: Hide the Edge Insider promotion
summary: No Edge Insider ad on Edge's About page.
what: Applies the Edge policy that stops the About Microsoft Edge page from promoting the Edge Insider preview channels.
benefit: A cleaner About page. It changes nothing else in Edge.
risk: None. Edge may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: A small tidy-up. Skip it if you do not mind the promotion.
facts: Only the About Microsoft Edge page is affected
Applies to every account
Revert removes the policy value

name: Stop Edge asking to be your default
summary: No prompts to make Edge the default browser and Bing the default search.
what: Applies the Edge policy that turns off the default browser settings campaign.
benefit: Edge stops asking to become your default browser and to make Bing your default search engine.
risk: None. Your current default browser and search engine are not changed. Edge may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested if Edge is not your main browser.
facts: Without the policy, Edge prompts when it is not the default or Bing is not the search
Edge 113 or later on Windows
Applies to every account
Revert removes the policy value

name: Send Microsoft only the required Edge data
summary: Optional browsing and crash data stays on your PC.
what: Applies the Edge policy that sets diagnostic data to required data only, which turns off the optional data.
benefit: Edge stops sending the optional data about how you use the browser, the sites you visit and crash reports.
risk: None for security. Required data is what Microsoft says keeps Edge secure, up to date and performing. Edge may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested for everyone who uses Edge. It leaves the required data on on purpose.
facts: Microsoft marks the Off value as not recommended, so Off is not used here
Edge 122 or later controls this on Windows 10 separately from Windows data
Takes effect after Edge restarts
Revert removes the policy value

name: Turn off Brave Rewards
summary: No Brave Rewards icon, ads or tokens.
what: Applies the Brave policy that disables Brave Rewards, the feature that pays users for ads they see.
benefit: Removes the Rewards icon and its ad notifications from Brave.
risk: Low. You cannot turn Rewards back on from inside Brave until you revert. Brave may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested if you do not use Brave Rewards. Skip it if you earn or give tokens.
facts: Brave's policy text says users cannot change or override it once set
Applies to every Brave profile on this PC
Revert removes the policy value

name: Turn off Brave Wallet
summary: No built-in crypto wallet in Brave.
what: Applies the Brave policy that disables Brave Wallet, the built-in crypto wallet.
benefit: Removes the wallet button and its code paths from Brave.
risk: Low. Do not use it if you keep crypto in Brave Wallet, since you could not open it until you revert. Brave may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested if you do not use Brave Wallet. Skip it if you do.
facts: Brave's policy text says users cannot change or override it once set
Applies to every Brave profile on this PC
Revert removes the policy value

name: Turn off Brave VPN
summary: No Brave VPN offer or button in Brave.
what: Applies the Brave policy that disables Brave VPN, the paid VPN built into the browser.
benefit: Removes the VPN button and its upsell from Brave.
risk: Low. Do not use it if you subscribe to Brave VPN. Brave may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested if you do not use Brave VPN. Skip it if you pay for it.
facts: Brave's policy text says users cannot change or override it once set
Applies to every Brave profile on this PC
Revert removes the policy value

name: Turn off Brave AI Chat
summary: No built-in AI assistant in Brave.
what: Applies the Brave policy that turns Brave's AI Chat assistant off.
benefit: Removes the assistant from the sidebar and the page summary prompts in Brave.
risk: Low. You cannot use AI Chat until you revert. Brave may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested if you do not use the assistant in Brave. Skip it if you do.
facts: Brave's policy text says users cannot change or override it once set
Applies to every Brave profile on this PC
Revert removes the policy value

name: Turn off Brave News and Brave Talk
summary: No news feed on the new tab page and no video call feature.
what: Applies the two Brave policies that disable Brave News and Brave Talk and hide their interface.
benefit: A plain new tab page with no curated news feed, and no Talk video call button.
risk: Low. You cannot use either until you revert. Brave may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested if you do not read the Brave News feed or make Brave Talk calls.
facts: Brave's policy text says all related interface elements are hidden
Two policy values are set, one for News and one for Talk
Applies to every Brave profile on this PC
Revert removes both policy values

name: Stop Brave's usage pings
summary: No anonymous usage ping and no product analytics from Brave.
what: Applies the two Brave policies that turn off the anonymous stats usage ping and Privacy Preserving Product Analytics (P3A).
benefit: Brave stops sending the usage ping it uses to count active users and the product analytics answers it collects.
risk: None. Brave's own text calls both anonymous. Brave may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested for everyone who uses Brave and wants less data leaving the PC.
facts: Brave describes both as anonymous and opt-in features it enables by default
Brave's policy text says users cannot change or override it once set
Applies to every Brave profile on this PC
Revert removes both policy values
